title: Make form feedback clearer with Motion Design
description: Try a local example, copy the tested brief and inspect an honest baseline comparison.
body:
Guides / Motion Design

Motion / reviewed 9 November 2026

Make interface
feedback feel clear.

Build loading, success and retry states in a small practice form, then check that they work for everyone.

One paired task test / both outputs passed

Before you start

You need a coding agent that reads local Markdown, a browser and a separate practice folder. This exercise uses explicit source context; native skill installation is not required or tested.

Download practice pack Try the finished demo →

The demo uses a made-up name and a local 800ms simulation. Nothing is booked or sent.

Set it up in four steps

  1. Keep a clean starting point

    Unzip into a new folder. Preserve sample/index.html; ask your agent to write a separate result.

  2. Give the agent the task

    Supply the sample and task.md. Explain that the result must stay self-contained with no external packages, storage or network calls.

  3. Add the reviewed guidance

    Supply source/skills/motion-design/SKILL.md and its local state-feedback and context-adaptation references. Ask the agent to read them before editing. Accessibility and task restrictions take precedence. Do not run installers or source examples.

  4. Open the result

    Open the generated HTML in a browser. Read the agent's notes and repeat the checks below.

Exact task brief
Improve the motion and interaction feedback in the accompanying `index.html`. The result
should feel calm, responsive and clear to someone reserving a practice workshop spot.

Keep the existing content, layout purpose and form functionality. Use plain HTML/CSS/JS in
one self-contained file with no external assets, imports, dependencies, network calls, storage
or accounts. Do not execute package installers or source examples. Preserve the existing IDs,
form `data-state` values (idle/loading/success/error), and 800ms local reservation simulation.
You may improve semantics, styling and implementation while preserving that test interface.

Provide appropriate hover, press, loading, success, validation-error and retry feedback.
Keep keyboard operation and visible focus. Honour `prefers-reduced-motion`; equivalent
information must remain available without movement. Avoid distracting persistent decorative
motion, layout movement that harms interaction, or feedback conveyed only by animation.
Keep a usable narrow mobile layout. State the motion choices and any limitations briefly.

Produce `index.html` and `notes.json` in the assigned output folder. The notes fields are
`motion_intent`, `changes`, `checks_performed`, `known_limits`, and `sources_used`.
Do not invent checks: source inspection is not browser execution. Do not read other experiment
outputs or change the input files. Use only your assigned starting file, this brief and any
explicitly supplied condition-specific reference material.

Verify your result

  • Tab through every control; submit blank input and check the explanation and focus.
  • Enter "Sam," choose Afternoon and submit. Loading must block duplicate submissions and success must confirm the session.
  • Enable the simulated error, submit, disable it and retry successfully.
  • Enable reduced motion and repeat. All information must remain clear.
  • Narrow the window: controls must fit and focus stay visible.

Fix or undo

If files cannot be read, check your agent's documented file-access method. If it proposes packages, restate the self-contained requirement. Keep failed attempts and label repairs. To undo, remove your separate practice folder after saving anything you want.

Our recorded comparison was a tie: both outputs passed the same checks. One pair does not establish an advantage. See the comparison.

What was tested, source and security limits

What this example proves

Two fresh GPT-6.1 Sol agents received the same starting file and task. One additionally read the reviewed skill references. Headless Microsoft Edge on Windows checked both frozen outputs, including a 390px viewport. Neither a beginner attempt nor independent human reproduction was performed.

Inspect the recorded browser checks (JSON). Frame rate, screen-reader experience, aesthetic preference, user completion and generation cost were not measured.

Source, cost and security details

LottieFiles Motion Design 1.0.0, commit f9a8a041b85185ee4881b3471d3415e939aac772. Pinned original source; MIT notice retained in the pack. The licence does not cover your assistant subscription costs. Existing agent access was used; allowance consumption and generation costs are unknown.

A separate AI reviewer inspected 19 source files and their hashes, allowing only this bounded text-context trial. This was not human security certification. SkillSpector did not run: its installation was blocked by a required dependency. Scanner findings remain unknown. Native installation and automatic triggering were not tested.

title: Normal request vs Motion Design
description: One matched task, thirteen checks and no established comparative advantage.
body:
Comparison · 9 November 2026

Does an extra skill help this task?

For this practice reservation form, a competent normal request matched Motion Design on every recorded check.

One paired generation · GPT-6.1 Sol · Windows / headless Edge

Observed results for this task only
Check groupNormal agentWith Motion Design
Critical checks12 / 1212 / 12
Idle-motion check1 / 11 / 1
Critical failures observed00

Checks covered preserved content, keyboard order and focus, blank validation, loading, duplicate submissions, timed success, failure/retry, reduced motion, narrow layout, runtime errors, external requests and idle movement.

No advantage established. No tier awarded. The skill-assisted version used a documented motion vocabulary and small feedback arrival; the baseline used simpler feedback. These choices do not prove better usability.

Try the guide Read recorded checks ·

How future tiers will work

  • S — Repeated benefit: at least three matched pairs, all critical checks passed, acceptance no worse than baseline and a demonstrated task-relevant benefit.
  • A — Useful alternative: task-tested critical checks pass; repeated advantage is not yet established.
  • B — Limited fit: observed limitations restrict useful cases; explain the fallback.

Eligibility is not an automatic award. Source-only editorial picks stay separate; insufficient evidence stays unranked. Severe unresolved risk blocks recommendation. We compare tools within a task, never all skills on one universal leaderboard.

How we test and report limits

title: How we choose
description: Sources, security review and task performance are different kinds of evidence.
body:
Our method · 9 November 2026

Useful claims need visible evidence.

A popular video is a lead. A working result is evidence for a specific task. Neither is a universal safety certificate.

  1. Trace the source. Find the original author, exact revision, licence and requirements.
  2. Review access and risk. Inspect instructions and dependencies before trying them. Separate unresolved risks from missing task evidence.
  3. Define success first. Prepare synthetic inputs, critical checks and a competent normal-agent baseline.
  4. Compare fairly. Use matched tasks, fresh contexts and equivalent checks. Preserve failures; publish sample sizes and unknowns.
  5. Write a repeatable guide. Include costs, setup, checks, limitations and removal. Retest changed revisions.

Evidence labels

Source reviewed means inspected documentation. Setup tested means one recorded setup worked. Task tested means inputs, outputs and checks exist. Independently reproduced requires a second person's successful attempt.

Our first trial's limits

Motion Design was supplied as explicit text context, without native installation. A separate AI review covered the source; SkillSpector was not run because its installation failed on a required dependency. Scanner findings are unknown.

One paired trial passed the same checks in both conditions. No independent human reproduction, beginner study or measured usability advantage exists. See the actual comparison.

title: هل حسّنت Motion Design النتيجة؟
description: ملخص عربي لتجربة واحدة: نجحت النسختان في الفحوص نفسها، دون إثبات تفوّق.
body:
مقارنة · ٩ نوفمبر ٢٠٢٦

هل تحتاج هذه المهمة إلى مهارة إضافية؟

في نموذج حجز تدريبي، نجحت استجابة عادية جيدة ومهارة Motion Design في الفحوص نفسها. لم تثبت التجربة تفوّق المهارة.

Read the English comparison

نتائج تجربة مقارنة واحدة
الفحوصالطلب العاديمع المهارة
الفحوص الأساسية١٢ من ١٢١٢ من ١٢
غياب الحركة المشتتة أثناء الانتظار١ من ١١ من ١

شملت الفحوص لوحة المفاتيح، والتحقق من الاسم، والتحميل، والنجاح، والخطأ وإعادة المحاولة، وتقليل الحركة، والعرض الضيق. الحجز محاكاة محلية؛ لا تُرسل بيانات ولا يُحجز موعد فعلي.

لا تصنيف ممنوح. هذه محاولة واحدة لكل حالة، وليست دراسة مستخدمين أو دليلاً على فائدة متكررة.

استخدمت الحالتان GPT-6.1 Sol، وفُحص الناتجان في Microsoft Edge على ويندوز. قُرئت المهارة كمرجع نصي؛ لم يُختبر تثبيتها أو تفعيلها تلقائياً. راجع وكيل ذكاء اصطناعي المصدر، لكن فحص SkillSpector لم يعمل بسبب تعذّر تثبيت أحد متطلباته. نتائج الفحص الأمني مجهولة.

لم تُقَس تجربة قارئ الشاشة أو سهولة الاستخدام أو تكلفة التوليد. ولم تُختبر سهولة استخدام هذه الصفحة العربية مع قارئ عربي مستقل.

title: About SkillLantern
description: Practical AI skill guides with clear sources and honest limits.
body:
About SkillLantern

Useful guidance.
Clear limits.

We help you choose AI capabilities and put them to work with practical guides, source notes and setup briefs.

Start with the task

A skill file is only a starting point. The result also depends on the agent, your context, tools, permissions and checks. Our guides make those pieces visible.

What we publish

Original source links, dated reviews and bounded examples. Source review, installation and measured task results are distinct. Read our evidence policy.

Your inputs stay with you

The setup planner runs in your browser. It does not send your answers to an AI service, store them in browser storage or save them automatically. You choose whether to copy or download a brief. The site has no analytics, account system or contact form. The hosting service may process routine request logs under its own policies.

Implementation support

Scoped setup help is a proposed next step, with pricing and availability undecided. See the proposed approach.

Editorial and privacy information updated 14 November 2026.
